utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this could the room. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Waespi or who is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Saklaine Hedaraly for the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, are you ready to call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We are, Your Honour. The Prosecution would like to call Mira Grubor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And fortunately, Ms. Grubor, you're there already.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to you. Before you give evidence in this court the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text has been given to you by the usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. I noted that you spoke in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're free to choose the language in which you express yourself best. If you -- I don't know whether you intended to continue in English or whether you would like to speak B/C/S as we call it or -- please be aware that if you have any hesitation as to whether you can express yourself in detail in the best way, please choose the language which is most suitable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Hedaraly, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Good morning. Could you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: My full name is Mira Grubor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And in what country do you presently reside?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I reside in New Zealand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And what is your occupation in New Zealand?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I'm a police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you recall being interviewed by representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor on 3 April 1998 and providing a statement to them?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you have a chance to review the statement in the last week?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did that statement accurately reflect to the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor on 3 April 1998?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And do you recall providing a supplemental statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on 12 July 2007?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I do recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And did you have a chance to review this supplemental statement in the last week?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And did -- and did that statement accurately reflect what you said to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: It does reflect.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could ask for 65 ter number 4779 to be brought up, and if I could provide a hard copy to the witness of her two statements so she can see them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The 65 ter number you mentioned, is that the first statement? Is that the 1998 statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes. And 4780 will be the 2007 statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first start with 4779.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And could we mark those for identification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, 4779 would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour that becomes Exhibit P54 marked for identification. And 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] for the 1998 statement. And then.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 04780, that's the 2007 statement, becomes Exhibit P55 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Ms. Grubor, this statement that in front of you the one dated 3 April 1998, is that the statement that you provided to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And the contents of that statement are true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and recollection?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if you asked the same questions today as you were asked in 1998 would you give the same answers?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the record we see at this moment the cover pages of the same but without signature. If it could be moved up a tiny little bit. Yes. That's clear. Yes. I see that the English statement is a signed statement. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I would like to have Exhibit P54 entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? No objections. P54 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And Ms. Grubor if I could now refer you to your 2007 statement?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Is that the statements you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor on July 2007.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And the contents of the supplemental statement are true to the best of your knowledge and recollection?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if you asked the same questions today that you were asked in 2007, would you give the same answers?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would like P55 to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there are no objections and I see no objections, hear no objections then P55 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note would you kindly make a second's pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could also mark for identification the two attachments to the supplemental statement which are 65 ter number 1584 and 1585 and have those admitted as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, 1584 would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes P56 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And P1585.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit P57 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections against these attachment to the statement? Then P56 and P57 are admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Ms. Grubor in the course of your 3 April 1998 interview, did you make markings and annotations on an aerial photograph of Knin?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could have 65 ter number 3747 pulled up and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 3747. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That becomes Exhibit P58 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could provide a hard copy of this map for the witness for ease of reference because we will be referring to it during examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. And that is an aerial photograph with some handwritten --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have some extra copies for the Court if you would like to have the hard copy for ease of reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a hard copy here. I notice, however, that the witness has a bigger sized.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I have a larger one to see, if you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I would also be grateful if we could get a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I got something -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can explain. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I received on my desk two different versions of 3747. The one I receive it now with a legend in red type written, and there is another one which seems to be the handwritten version of the same without translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. Because the contrast on the first map was not clear we just got it reproduced. We sent it to the Defence and we'll just confirm with the witness that those are the same markings before admitting it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's certainly is helpful comparing the two versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Ms. Grubor, does the -- does the map that you have been given, Exhibit P58, does this map reflect the annotations you made in your 3 April 1998 statement?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: As far as I can recall it's the same one, just much clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage we would like to admit Exhibit P58 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections against P58?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then P58 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to read out a short summary of the evidence of this witness contained in the two statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Does the witness know why we're doing this?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, but if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Grubor, we do it so that your written statement, which we've read, that at least the public, and this is a public hearing, knows what it is all about. Please proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mira Grubor was born in the hamlet of Grubori in the Knin municipality. When Operation Storm began on 4 August 1995, she was a laboratory assistant at the Knin hospital. On that day while at the hospital, she observed a number of persons brought to the hospital that had been killed and injured by the shelling of the town. On the first day, about 120 dead bodies, among which approximately 30 to 40 in civilian clothes were brought to the hospital. Another 160 to 180 injured people were also brought to the hospital on that day, and approximately 40 to 60 of those wore civilian clothing. As far as Ms. Grubor can remember, all the dead and injured brought to the hospital on the 4th of August had been killed or injured because of the shelling. In the early morning of the 5th of August, Ms. Grubor drove to the UN camp with a doctor from the hospital to seek the UN's assistance in taking the seriously wounded persons back to the UN compound. Later that morning at around 10.30, Croatian soldiers entered the hospital and Ms. Grubor fled to the UN camp. This concludes my summary, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hedaraly. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Ms. Grubor, I'm going to ask you a few questions to clarify the statements that you've given us and that have been entered into evidence. In your first statement, P54, on the second paragraph you said that six days before Operation Storm began you sent your daughter to Serbia after the fall of Grahovo. My first question is, first of all, how old was your daughter at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: She was five at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber what were the specific reasons for sending her away to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: After Bosanska Grahovo was taken over by Croatian soldiers, the Knin and the Krajina were cut off from Serbia, meaning cut off from supply in food or anything else. I did not want my daughter to experience any lack of food or hardship, so I decided to send her over until I work out what's happening, what's going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Was there any other reasons -- any other reason to send her?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: No. The other reason is the safety. I was afraid what may have happened next after Grahovo was taken over.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you have any -- any specific -- did you have any specific fears of what may happen?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw withdrawal of is Serbian soldiers from Grahovo after Grahovo was taken over. I just had a fear that the very next step maybe another attack towards my place, Knin, and I did not want my five-year-old daughter to be there present if that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And how long did you plan to be separated from your daughter?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: For a start, I thought probably about a week, two weeks maximum. Just until I realise what is happening, what is going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And what was your plan after? Was it to join her in Serbia or to have her come back to Knin?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Depending on the circumstances. If it was safe for her to come back I would bring her back, but if it wasn't then definitely in two weeks' time maximum I would make my way and join her in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 4 of that statement, P54, the first paragraph at the top. In the middle of the paragraph there is a statement: "There were no RSK military positions in Knin ..." What did you mean by military positions?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Within last few days prior to this event I did not see any, let's say, large military group, soldiers, in the town. There were very few of them to be seen on the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And can you please tell us what was the composition of the town on 4 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I can refer to probably couple days prior to that and on the very 4th. The -- the town itself looked rather deserted. At the time the buses were not running any more, so only people who lived in the town -- in the town were there, and I would say probably mostly women and civilians who lived in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 3, the previous page of P54. In the second paragraph you mention two incidents that were particularly horrifying, and I just want to clarify the source of your knowledge for both of these incidents. Let's start with the first, the elderly woman that had suffered from a stroke and that husband's -- that woman's husband and son were killed when the vehicle received a hit. Who told you about the vehicle being hit?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: When I was in the hospital and I saw elderly woman on the stretcher and a nurse attending, so I approached to ask if I could be of any help. The nurse told me that woman was brought by someone to hospital who said that woman's son and husband about to take her to hospital, then their vehicle was shot directly by -- the bomb fell directly onto the vehicle killing husband and son.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I want to move to the second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I could just note for the record our objection to the double hearsay nature of the statement, but I understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- if you have any objection against a question you may arise. What the Chamber will have to do with this double hearsay evidence, there's no reason to interrupt the flow of evidence for that reason. That can be done at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let's move to the second incident in that paragraph when you said that the vehicle was hit by shrapnel just outside the hospital. In this case, who told you that this incident had taken place right outside the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Again that incident -- during that incident I was inside in the hospital. I could see the entrance, main entrance of the hospital from the corridor, and I saw two males enter the hospital. One was carrying another one. The one who was carrying another man was yelling and shouting something like, "They killed him. He's dead." I did not know immediately what was happening, but then he said as they pulled outside the hospital the bomb fell nearby and shrapnel went through the back door and killed the man at the back. I did not go to see that myself. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: -- did see the hole on the car to support that. There was a hole on that vehicle that was outside the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Just to clarify. So you could see that from inside the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes. Hospital entrance was big glass door. I could see that through the glass door as the vehicle was literally probably three metres outside away from the front entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you work at the hospital for the entire week preceding the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you at any time during that week see a RSK tank near the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Not in my recollection. I can't remember seeing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Could you -- when you would go to the hospital and when you were in the hospital, would you be able to see the whole vicinity of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I would say probably 70, 80 per cent of hospital grounds, meaning south side, west, and north side. Probably east side would be blocked because the entrance probably was from the west side of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And as far as you can remember, when was the last time that you saw an RSK tank in the city of the Knin?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, that was on the day when Bosansko Grahovo was taken over by Croatian army. I saw a convoy of trucks and tanks and cannons coming back to the town from Bosansko Grahovo direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can turn to your supplemental statement, P55, at paragraph 10, page 3. There's a reference there in the middle of the paragraph about Croatian tanks were also firing in the town. Did you find the reference?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's here. You can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber when, where, in what circumstances you saw these Croatian tanks firing in the town?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: The first time I hear the tanks firing that was on the 5th of August. We were working on the transport of our wounded outside the hospital just in front of the morgue when a series of loud explosions, firing, began. It was different than previous shelling. It was much powerful, louder, and I am pretty sure it was tanks firing the targets around. I can't tell exactly what the target was at the time, but it was very close, and very terrifying experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So just to clarify, you did not actually see the tank, but you heard fire from what you thought were tanks?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right. I did not see them at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And at what time was that? You said in the 5th August --

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: 5th of August. I think it was about 9.00. I may be wrong for half an hour before or later, but I'm pretty sure it was 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can go back to your first statement, P54. On page 4, the third paragraph. You discuss the arrival of Croatian soldiers at the hospital. Now, do you know if the soldiers fired any shots inside the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes. When they arrived I was outside the hospital. I saw them. I hear them at the -- at the gate, hospital gate. I ran downstairs into the bomb shelter, and few minutes after that I could hear swearing upstairs and then yelling, and then I could hear shots being fired. I hear the explosion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure what happened after that because that's when I took off from hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I didn't want to object earlier, but some of the questions that are being asked here, including whether there was a tank in front of the hospital and now whether there were gunshots, et cetera, don't appear in her statements and look to me have been discussed with the witness prior to her appearance here. We have not received a proofing statement so these are all matters that are new to us and I feel a little hindered in cross-examination that matters are being raised for the first time with the witness on the stand that we have not gotten notice of.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the reference to the RSK tank was raised by the Defence as late as Friday, and we only talked to the witness last night, and it seems to me that they all fall within the ambit of clarifying the statement whether there were shots. She says that the Croatian soldiers came in. They were pointing their guns. The logical clarification question whether any shots were fired from these guns. So we don't think that that's necessarily hindering the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, tank of course is a bit different. I take it you're aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The issue there is clearly whether there was any counter-fire attracted by certain activities. So it would have been appropriate if you would have given notice to the Defence specifically on that issue which goes beyond just clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It's noted, Mr. President. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: At the -- at the bottom of the same page, in the last paragraph on P54, on the first line when you went to -- back to the town to -- to your friend's apartment, you said: "On the house there was a notice that it was occupied." Can you please tell us if you remember what the notice actually said?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: When we approach the house, on the front door, on one big piece of board, there was a sign saying "This house is occupied by --" I think it was short form of -- like it was HVO: "This house is occupied by HVO member." But I'm not absolutely sure what exactly, whether there was a name or more text, but it was quite common to see during those days such notices on the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: In the same paragraph, on the last line when you encountered a group of men and you say the men threatened you and your friend and you had to leave, in the last line, just tell us what was the threat, the specific threat that was made?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: My friend that was with me was not happy about her house being occupied, and she started complaining loudly about it. I could see the group of young people, probably about 30, 40 metres away. There were two females and three or four males on the street. As she was complaining and saying that no one has had the right to get into her house and take away her property, one of the males from the group could hear that. He started arguing back saying something like, "Do you know who you are? You have no right here." Something along those lines. And then friend of mine continued to argue. The next moment three males started running towards us threatening, and we just managed to get into the car. And as we were leaving, the first man managed to reach the vehicle. He literally bumped into the vehicle trying to open the door which we locked as soon as we got inside, and we took off.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to turn my attention now to the shelling that you described in your previous statements, and I will refer you to your annotations made on the aerial photo of Knin. That's Exhibit P58. In particular, I want to focus on some of the areas labelled on the map as areas of shelling that you saw. I'm not sure we'll be able to go through all of them, but I just want to discuss a few of them with you. The first one is the area that you labelled as number 6. Can you please tell the Court what is it that you saw being shelled in that area?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: This building circled by number 6, on the 5th of August in the morning I was on my way to the UN camp with doctor. We were going to ask for help with wounded in the hospital. As we were passing -- as we passed over the railway bridge, I looked up and I could see through the window, side window, the building. I could see big hole in the ceiling. I actually could see the sky above.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And what was -- what was that building that you saw?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: At the ground floor of this building there was a shoe store. The top floor was residential apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Was there any military presence either on that -- on the days preceding this shoe store?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Not as far as I remember. Not around -- not in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. On that trip to the UN compound did you notice any other shelling?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: The shelling was permanent, and it was all the way as we left the hospital. Ahead of us, around, you know, on either side of the road. And even when we entered the town, I could not see explosions any more, but I could hear them. When we nearly reach the UN camp, just as soon as we cross Krka River I saw a bomb to fell onto a convoy of vehicles and tractors where people were waiting obviously for the bombing to cease to pass through the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I believe that's in your supplemental statement. On your return from -- from the UN camp after your first visit did you notice any other shelling or any difference between your first trip and your return trip?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: On our way back, again as soon as we crossed the railway bridge, probably about 50 to 100 metres ahead there was a big hole in the middle of the road which was not there on our way down to the UN camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time if we can have 65 ter number 3759. And it's only seven seconds of that clip that I would like to be marked for identification at this time, from 15 minutes 55 seconds to 16 minutes and 2 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any text spoken on this clip?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There isn't. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P59 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Is this the road you say when you saw a shell?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That hole was right -- well, actually on the left of this vehicle which can be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And how -- how large was that hole in the middle of the road?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: It's -- it's hard to tell. I would say probably -- could be between -- anything between half metre to one metre in diameter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we ask perhaps the witness with the cursor to point at where exactly she sees the hole. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That was my next question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I was just going to ask if we could get some guidance as to which number this is on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's going to be my next question just raised by Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So first if the witness could draw our attention to where the hole could be seen on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If the map could be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course this is a video.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If the map could be placed on the ELMO so the witness can refer to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I have two different questions. The one is where this location is in town. My question specifically to the witness would be -- yes. Could I just see -- Ms. Grubor, could I ask you on this picture on the screen at this moment do you see the hole you were describing before, the hole in the road.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand specifically when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you told us -- let me just -- you're asked: "Is this the road," after the video had been played, "when you saw a shell?" I take it that you were asked where you saw a shell. And then you said, "Yes, it is -- the hole was right -- well, actually on the left of this vehicle which can be seen." Now, what can be seen, the vehicle can be seen or the hole can be seen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And not the hole.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The vehicle on the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And not the hole.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And not the hole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. The next thing was whether you could point on this map that you've marked and the revised version where exactly this is. Did you mark it by any number?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, not. Then we would invite the witness to -- Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to again object. She's now being asked about targets that are not on her map and have not been disclosed in any proofing statement or anything which hinders our ability to cross-examine. This is the first time this is being raised with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I believe that when the witness will show on the map it was right around one the areas that was shelled. It's a clarification question in what was in the area and what specifically was there and what she saw being hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't mind, Your Honour, clarification with the witness but when they clarify and then don't disclose the clarification it not only hinders our ability, but it also hinders the Trial Chamber's ability to get all the facts and we're going to have to cross-examine today without the benefit of having prepared on these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's fair that if a witness marks a map with a lot of places where, as the -- as the legend says where shelling was seen, then of course it comes a bit of a surprise where we have there listed five such incidents that suddenly in examination-in-chief a sixth is added to it. I take it the Defence has done some investigative work on what it may finds at places 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11, and of course could not prepare for this. First let's ask the witness where we are at this moment but this certainly is a matter that should better be taken care of in the near future and for the time being, we'll proceed and we'll also see whether there's any need for the Defence to -- to get additional time. Could the witness first indicate on this map, that is map P58, where this street, where next to the car a shell landed or whether she saw a hole there. Could you tell us where that is? Perhaps first -- is there a possibility to have P58 or do we have it on the screen at this moment? No. We have -- could we get P58 on the screen again? Yes. But now preferably the version which is the version -- I see here we have two versions of the document, and now the -- I think we need the other one. That is the one with typewritten --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps it would be simpler to have the witness place the map on the ELMO and we can refer to it for the record that way and when she identifies the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that would not allow us to -- if that would be a good thing to do, that would not allow the witness to mark the place and then that could be stored as a new exhibit. That is the -- we would lose that opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I believe, Your Honour, that we'll be able to make the record clear enough with respect to other markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, of course, I'm a bit concerned, if I ask for P58 and I get a document different from the one I consider to be P58, that is of some concern. That could not be just repaired by putting something on the ELMO. Mr. Registrar, is there -- or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that we can assist Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just ask you. I know you told us about a second and more clear version of P58, but that one appears not to have been uploaded in e-court, although we got a hard copy of that version.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It's upload at number 4832, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I then take it that P58 will now be the document which is uploaded at 4832, and that now will become P58. Yes. Now we have it on our screen. Perhaps could we ask the witness where on this map the street is located where we saw the car and where you said there was a hole next to that car. If you could start with the cursor. Is -- does that now indicate the place where we saw that car, Ms. Grubor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's on the right from circle labelled number 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just on the right of the circle labelled number 10, and that is in the close vicinity to the bridge of the railway. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, that's on the way back as soon as I passed the bridge over the railway. It's somewhere -- we used to call this place on the left small market, and there on the middle of the road somewhere was big hole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: How far away from the bridge was that -- was that hole?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I'm not that good at distance, but I would say probably couple hundred metres or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can turn to the area labelled as number 4 on your map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, this is an aerial photograph. Do we have a scale somewhere so that we can --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I don't believe that there is one on the -- on the photograph itself, but I'm sure that we can provide one for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you could try to agree with the Defence that if we see aerial photographs, and especially if distances are asked from witnesses, that it -- it says "No scale available" on the bottom, but if it's not available you should take care that you get it. And I take it that there are ways of getting a scale into this map. By knowing distances you can measure them, you can set them out on such a map, so that we know what we are talking about. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And turning to the area labelled 4 which you had marked as the police station, when did you see this police station being shelled?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: It was late in night, in between 4th and 5th. I remember it was late, probably about 1.00 in the morning, and I saw that big blaze, explosion, down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And where were you when you saw -- you saw this?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I was in hospital, and -- and what draw our attention was it was night-time. It was just a big -- a number of serial explosions, and -- like big blaze coming from that direction. I could not tell it was a police station as it was far away, but it was coming from that direction, and my common sense was telling me it could be only police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If I can turn your attention to the area that you had circled as number 8. Can you -- can you please tell the Trial Chamber where you were and what you observed more specifically?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Most of the shelling I observed on the 4th of August as most of the day I spent in hospital. I have to say again that I had a better view of hill areas rather than flat areas. I saw bombs falling all over the place and just below the castle hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So was area 8 -- the area you circled at 8 on P58 a hill area?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, that was a hill area and that's why I could see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if you could tell the Court what is generally in that area?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: That's residential houses all this area from -- almost from point 6 up to this circle 8. It's mostly residential area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Were there any -- any shops, any restaurants, any cafes in that area in addition to houses?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I can't -- the only restaurant that I know of that's -- that's -- there was a restaurant in the very castle. As soon as you enter the castle there was a restaurant on the left, but not in this area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And was there -- was there -- did you see at any time, let's say, in the week before the 4th of August, any military presence in the area that you circled as 8 on Exhibit P58?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I can answer that question simply because I was not coming frequently up to that area. Our main road was the place where all of us were having shops or restaurants or bus station, but number 8 is a bit out of the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And could you see the main road from when you went to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Sorry, can you repeat that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Of course. From that vantage point at the hospital could you see that main road or the area just below where you circled number 8?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: No, no. No, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If I could ask you similar questions with respect to area number 10. Where -- once again, where were you and what did you see more specifically?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Same again. I was in the hospital. Number 10 is also a bit rised on the hill, and that's why I had a good clear view of place from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Is the hospital also slightly elevated?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yeah, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And I'm just going to ask you for area 10. What kind of area was that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Residential houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Only residential areas, only residential houses?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Was there any -- did you notice any military presence in the days preceding August 4th in that area?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: No. No. Friend of mine lived there. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's all I have, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hedaraly. Before I give an opportunity to cross-examine the witness, I would like to seek some clarification, a few points. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Grubor -- yes. In your 1998 statement, you explain that you sent your daughter to Belgrade, and you -- in the statement it says the following: "There were rumours going around that the Croats will attack us, but there were also rumours that the Serbs will try to regain control of Bosansko Grahovo. When the shelling started, my first thought was that the latter was now taking place." That is, the Serbs regaining. Today in your testimony you said, when asked whether you had any specific fears, you said, "Yes, I did. I saw withdrawal of Serbian soldiers from Grahovo after Grahovo was taken over. I just had a fear that the very next step may be another attack towards my place, Knin, and I did not want my five-year-old daughter to be there present if that happened." Now, from what I understand, at that moment Knin was still Serb-controlled area.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So in your written statement on the one hand you say, "What I had expected as a matter of fact was -- first thing I expected was a Serb attack rather than a Croatian attack," whereas in your testimony today when asked about a specific fear you're referring to a Croatian attack on Knin rather than a Serb effort to regain Grahovo.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Not this exactly. This statement was -- this was -- I sent my daughter away about six days prior to the event of -- that took place on 4th of August. However, probably two, three days prior to this event there were rumours that there is going to be a major counter-attack by Serbs on Croats' positions in order to get Grahovo back and other areas. However, that was just probably two or three days before this event took place, and majority of the male population, soldiers, I mean all of them were in soldiers, were sent away towards Bosnia from our area. So that's when the bombing started. I was not sure whether it was artillery, fire done by Serbs from somewhere or by Croats. That was 5.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What you say is that the situation, expectations, and circumstances changed very quickly in that period of time, which also had an impact on what you expected to happen.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Of course it did, because as I said, the last couple days prior to this event -- during the wartime all of us are hoping for the best, for something to end up, for something to come to resolution, and everyone is hoping for best for him, but, however, there were rumours that Serbs are going to take over Grahovo and few other places in order to get stability and security, let's say, road towards Serbia which at the time was our only supply of everything in Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Totally different question, very short one. You explained to us what happened and what you saw from the glass doors --

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of the hospital when elderly come came in with a severe stroke and what happened, the car being hit. Could you remember what time of the day that was?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I would say on Thursday, sometime afternoon. I know it was not dark yet. It was probably about -- between 2.00 and 4.00 afternoon, but I can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may just clarify for the record. There were two incidents, the one with the glass door was not the elderly woman. There were the two men that were taken. I think the witness understood the question, but just to clarify the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'm mistaken there. Yes, yes. I'm -- yes. It's not about the elderly lady. The incident that took place between the 2.00 and 4.00 you were referring to --

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: To the glass door.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the car. A glass door where you saw a car and you saw the car being damaged --

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Outside the hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- outside the hospital yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I could just clarify I'm not sure that she said it was being damaged in front of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We could check that, but what exactly happened to the car I think she said there was a hole in the car, but I'll check that. It is at least clear that's what you saw when you were behind the glass doors with 78 per cent of view on the hospital premises. Then my last question is: You were asked about paragraph 10 of your 2007 statement, and I read it slowly to you. You said in the statement: "I don't even remember seeing any RSK vehicle. I saw a few soldiers walking around the city but no group or organised group of soldiers." I understood this as a reference to RSK soldiers, but if that's wrongly understood please tell me.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: That's RSK soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Misetic, from the fact that you're on your feet I take it that the agreed order of cross-examination is that the Gotovina Defence starts first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Grubor, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Misetic, who is counsel for Mr. Gotovina. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Grubor.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just some background clarification. You indicated that you are today a police officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You were not a police officer in 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you have any type of police training in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In terms of your training as a police officer today, are you involved in investigative work as a police officer? Criminal investigative work.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I joined the police force in New Zealand three years ago, mainly spending last three years on front line. Just recent, two, three months I am into family violence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Family violence.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you, the expression "front line" is known to me in military terms, not specifically in police terms. May I take it that it is patrolling on the street, being out rather than being behind your desk.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. That is responding to calls, incident responding, which is shift work and any kind of job, urgent job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. It's just my ignorance in this field. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Both the Prosecution and the Trial Chamber asked you some questions about your decision to send your daughter to Serbia. You said it was six days before Operation Storm, so would it be safe to say that it was 30 July 1995 when you sent your daughter?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I can't remember the date. I know it was -- I think it was Saturday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Prior to those events.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And how did your daughter make it to Serbia, by what means of transportation?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: There was some road which was not official road to leave Knin and go through the area of Lika. I never went that road myself. It -- later I learned it was not even asphalt road. It was a metal road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But what means of transportation did she take?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Every -- there was a bus. Every morning bus was leaving Knin going to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And were many people putting families on these buses to take them to Serbia, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I would say there were probably about 150 people more around the bus. So I would say if the bus takes about 50 people, probably out of those 150 I would say probably 100 of them wanted to least area, but there was no enough place in the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Were you told that people were putting their families on buses and sending them to Serbia before you decided to send your daughter?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: That fall of Grahovo, it was Friday in my recollection. I ask hospital driver to take me to my village to take my daughter as a woman next door, a neighbour, had already booked the ticket on that bus for Serbia. I ask her for a favour to take my daughter with her and just to contact my brother and give him my daughter until I see what is happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Were you aware prior to your decision to put your daughter on the bus that Mr. Martic had declared a state of war?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I thought that there was a state of war declared five years earlier, in 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But that there was another official proclamation after the fall of Grahovo by the so-called RSK government?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: If it was, I don't know of. It maybe, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You spoke in answer to the Presiding Judge's question concerning the events in Grahovo, you said that the soldiers were going towards Bosnia, and in your statement you said that there were rumours that the Serbs will try to regain control of Bosansko Grahovo. Were you aware that there was a, in fact, a planned military operation known as Operation Dinara 95?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: As I said about two days prior to this event there were -- there were lots of rumours as all of us who lived in the area were scared and terrified after Grahovo was taken over, and there were rumours that soldiers of Krajina are going to Bosnia to regain control, to get all their territory back, but that's all just rumours, and I wouldn't be 100 per cent sure of what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You were working in the hospital, which is why I'm going to ask you these next few questions. Were you aware that around the 30th of July the RSK authorities had evacuated the village of Strmica of civilians and used that as a staging area for the military?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: No. I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Were there people that were perhaps moved that were coming into the hospital from Strmica around that time?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: All -- the only thing, it was since fall of Grahovo in relation to civilians, I have heard of some woman going to help to dig the shelters or something, channels somewhere, but I wouldn't even be able to tell where.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters notes please pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 7 of your 2007 statement you were asked about preparations that would be made about an attack. You said, for example, moving equipment and supplies in the basement. I would like you to show you a video clip right now. This is from the morning of the 4th of August. If you could take a look at this video, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before -- perhaps before we play it I would like to show from Mr. Hedaraly first whether the video clip that was shown to us earlier, was that the same video material we have looked at before and where we were -- at least it was suggested that there were two different versions of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It was a short clip from the video that was shown by the Gotovina Defence on -- last week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, was it the edited version or was it the raw material that was shown?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I believe it was the raw material, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was the raw material here. So we don't have to look behind every car to see whether there's -- because I heard there was some birds singing on that video and sound appears to be an important matter when looking at videos. So that's the raw material. That's clear. Now, the video that we're now looking at, Mr. Misetic, is what exactly? Where does it come from? If you prefer to first put it to the witness and then give the information that's fine as well as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If I may, I mean Mr. Misetic represented it was from the 4th so I think it makes more sense to have the source of the video --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I allowed specifically Mr. Misetic to first show it and first hear the answers of the witness, and I exactly did that in order to avoid any exercise of influence on the witness knowing the background of the video. So let's look at it. Let's hear the answers to the questions, and then we'll learn what the background --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's precisely why I wanted the witness to say if she could identify it for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the number is 1D14-0001, and if it could be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any text spoken on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We've eliminated the audio because we're just interested in the pictures, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar. That would be Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D68 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D68 exclusively the images and not any sound. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Ms. Grubor, were you able to watch the video?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The man that looked to be speaking in a white outfit, did you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can you identify for the Court who that is?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: That is Dr. Goran Jejina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And do you recognise the location where that was filmed?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did it look like the basement of the hospital to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: That looked like single -- those wires along the hall, but I was not there at the time of the attack. I was upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: On the 4th of August did you ever go to the basement of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Not into the operating room. We were all working as physical forces taking wounded down to the basement, leaving them there and going upstairs, taking the stretchers back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So you are aware then that the surgical room had been in the basement?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I knew they were doing all surgical requirements down in the basement. Everyone was evacuated from the upper floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Prior to the 4th of August was it usual to perform surgeries in the basement?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Why was -- why were surgeries being performed in the basement on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: The common sense would be as soon as the bombing started to take everyone down to the lower floors, basement, and bomb shelter in order to prevent -- to protect people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the basement was equipped with any supplemental power like a generator or something to that effect?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: We had during the wartime quite often power being cut. The generator would be used every time in hospital whenever there was a cut of power.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How much power could the generators supply? In other words, how -- let's me rephrase that. For how many days or hours could the generator supply power when the power was cut, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, this is a -- apparently a complex technical question which is introduced in a rather simple way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just if she knows from working in the hospital whether there was power for days or the generator would only work for half day and they would be without power in the hospital. Just from her basic knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All right. Let's first hear the answer of the witness and then I may say a few words about it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would never be able to answer that question. I know during that we in hospital during the wartime never run out of power and I knew that it was due to that generator, but I wouldn't know how long it could run.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have dealt with it, I'll tell you what my concern was. You're asking about a generator where usually it's about fuel rather than about generators not being able to perform for a longer period of time. So therefore by focusing on the generator you might implicitly ask for fuel conditions, which is of course a rather different matter. That's the reason why I -- I expressed some concern about the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm reminded to ask if we could have D68 admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D68. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we don't have any objection for the admission, but I think it would be helpful for everyone if we could have the sound of the video since someone is talking for the major part of it. But for the purpose --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know what he is telling us. I take it that has been disclosed to you, so you can check that with your language assistant -- has not been disclosed?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. We got it from the Prosecution, I believe, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore if the Defence says it's not relevant, well, if the text would be, well, it's hard work on this Christmas Day, then of course I may take it that the Prosecution has a specific interest in hearing that text, whereas as far as I understand the only thing we have done here is we have seen a doctor known to the witness in a place unknown to the witness although it might be the basement, and the witness telling us in the basement surgical activity took place. I rather have an issue on what rather than the relevance is in addition to what the witness told us, because she did not identify that specific place as the basement. It looks very much as a medical environment, but -- so therefore is there no objection then. Please check the sound and see whether there's anything interesting for you on it and then we'll hear from you. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Noted, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D68 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to change topics and I note this might be an appropriate time for the first break, but I will obviously following your guidance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we'd have the break now. We will resume at 5 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, if you're ready to continue, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Ms. Grubor, the Knin hospital was the main hospital in Sector South; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And it was the only hospital in Sector South that had a surgical ward?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that any seriously wounded people in Sector South requiring surgery would have [Realtime transcript read in error "been"] had to be transported to the Knin hospital?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, we talked about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask you, I understood you saying would have to be transported. Is that what you asked, or did I misunderstand you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Have to be transported, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but here it says would have been transported, which is not exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think I said would have to be transported.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would have to be transported. Which is that -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Hypothetically speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And would have been transported is more factual. Therefore, the transcript does not fully reflect your words, but it now does. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Registrar if we could call up 1D14-0002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, when it's being uploaded could you at the same time give us a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours that becomes Exhibit D69, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2 of this document. It is an Associated Press report from the 4th of August, and I believe it's paragraph 6. If we could blow that up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, obviously I don't know what question my colleague will ask, but I don't know if it makes sense for the witness to be -- to have a chance to look at the whole document for the context of, which will be asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It very much depends on the question. So therefore perhaps we should wait for the question then find out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will show her two documents, Your Honour. Actually, one document and then another piece of evidence and then ask her some questions about this topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't know if you can see that, but there is a one-sentence paragraph there that says: "The town hospital --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have it enlarged in such a way that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's paragraph 6, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "The town hospital, forced to operate from its basement, reported eight civilians brought in, one of whom died. Another man was reported killed in his car." And I would like to ask you related to this topic about how many people were killed, you indicate in your statement that you were -- you went with a Dr. Torbica to the UN compound on the morning of the 5th of August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you spoke to two gentlemen who appeared at the UN gate?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I did not talk to anyone. I said at time I did not speak English at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Was there translator?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: There was a translator Dr. Igor Torbica took charge and he spoke to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So were you able to follow the discussion through the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I can't remember to be honest. It was such a rush and panic that it was just briefly spoken and we left a few minutes afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, one of the UN peacekeepers in recounting your visit with them on the morning of the 5th told the Office of the Prosecutor, and I quote: "The Serb doctor that we spoke to the day before refused our help related to us a number of stories --" sorry let me put it in context. "It was about the same time that the Serb doctor from the day before approached the gate, and this time he was asking for our help rather than us offering the hospital help. The Serb doctor that we spoke to the day before refused our help, related to us a number of stories, and when we questioned him as to how many were killed or how many dead were in the hospital, he maintained that only seven people were killed during the offensive, which made both Colonel Leslie and myself sort of laugh at his story." My question for you, Ms. Grubor, is you were present for that discussion. Do you recall Dr. Torbica telling the UN that only seven people had been killed during the offensive?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember a discussion about how many people were killed?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: No simply because at the time Mr. Torbica communicated in English down there. Like I said I learned English once I emigrated to New Zealand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me show you a document. This is a protocol -- Mr. Registrar, it is 1D14-0145, and if we could get an exhibit number for us. It is a protocol prepared by the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia, which identifies all bodies buried in Sector South during, before and after Operation Storm including the locations that the bodies were found. Mr. President, I will advise you that the Prosecution has the document. I believe that the whole document has not been translated because it is 26 pages. So we translated just the first 16 names because we believe it's relevant to this cross-examination but the whole document has not been translated although it will be -- appear before you here in Croatian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear no objections in using this in this way, an only partially translated document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar for the record the B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I remember there has been some discussion I take it with the Chamber's staff about -- was it about this document? A list where the Chamber said that if at least the heading and the most important entries are translated that everyone would find its way through this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar the B/C/S ID is 1D14-0121.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it needs a number this document but before we assign a number to this one, could I ask whether there are any objections against the D69, that is the Associated Press report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm not sure that a question was put to the witness with respect to that, and she said she didn't know so I don't think there's a foundation for that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, reference was made to what was described in this report and to some extent the witness I think confirmed that a Serbian doctor had been speaking to, but that she was not able to follow that conversation. Now, Mr. Misetic, just a glance of that document shows that there is a lot of information on the document. I take it you are not seeking the Chamber to rely upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Burning houses and attacks and all these kind of things, and the number of shells that fell in the centre of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless you're seeking --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I can withdraw the exhibit if the -- if Your Honours don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D69 is vacated. It was an Associated Press report, not something to rely upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then so we now I take it Mr. Registrar that we have now -- this new Republic of Croatia Ministry of the Interior document would then be D69? Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that's correct. D69 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or could we already -- I see that there's no objections from the Prosecution, Mr. Hedaraly, so therefore it's D69 now the new document is admitted into evidence please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour just as a technical matter should I wait for the Croatian version to be put on the screen as well? I'm sorry I'm advised it has to be linked, so I'll proceed with the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Ms. Grubor, in the protocol prepared by the Croatian government there were 16 bodies found in the Knin hospital when Croatian authorities arrived. You were in the hospital on that day. Do you recognise the names of any of these people as having been brought to the hospital on the 4th?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I don't recognise any of the names here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The status of the person as at least identified by the Croatian authorities is also -- also appears on this document. Do you have any reason to challenge the classification or the status of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Are there any people that you know of by name or otherwise that were killed and in the hospital on the 4th that do not appear on this list?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. What do you mean that were killed in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sorry. Any bodies that you know of that were in the Knin hospital on the 4th and who do not appear on this list, assuming of course that you know the names of such people?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I would know the names only -- only of the people that were transported with -- with us to the UN camp. If you ask me for the names of wounded, I would not know any of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I mean, who were submitted in hospital that they -- except other ones which I learn later on in UN camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: When patients were brought to the hospital on the 4th of August would you -- let me clarify further. Would the hospital staff record the names of those patients to the extent possible?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: To the extent that the person was brought in already deceased to the hospital, would the hospital staff attempt to identify the deceased?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I wouldn't know about that one. I was taking care of wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, just for my understanding, these questions, are they put to the witness in order to establish that this witness would not be aware of any more than 16 persons being killed and found in the Knin hospital on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm about to ask her questions to that effect, Your Honour, because it is our position that 16 were found in the hospital when Croatian authorities arrived, and now I'd like to explore with her the basis if -- the basis that she may have for a higher --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The last question whether there was any reason she would think of any other person. I don't know whether you were aware, but the question was put to you whether in your recollection the number of persons killed and found on the 4th of August in Knin hospital was limited to 16 or whether there more.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not work in the morgue. I was not there. Twice when I was passing by the door was not locked properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
