"Dr. Viskovic: At the moment the surgical service, the internist service, and general practice are in operation. As we go along other specialist services will be developed. "Journalist: Part of the personnel is the well-oiled team of the wartime hospital in Siska, which assisted in delivering the first baby girl born in Knin. These doctors have had a lot of experience in wartime work since 1991 and they say Knin is not their last stop. "Dr. Lozo: Our wartime career started in 1991 on the aisle of Pag then we worked at Velebit and continued to work there until now when we came to put into operation this beautiful facility. All of us had sworn an oath back in 1991 that we will end our war work in Vukovar. "Journalist: The nurse in this team is Danica Soric a native of Vukovar, who remembers the abuse suffered at the hands of Serbs after the town was occupied. "Ms. Soric: I was just telling my colleagues who were in Knin when we arrived. They were terrified. They must have been any of misinformed. I told them then how we felt and how we were treated when Vukovar was they said liberate, we'd call it captured and that's the way they treated us from start as prisoners, not as health care workers. It doesn't stand comparison. "Journalist: Around half of all medics and paramedics of Serbs who have worked here since before the operation. We have a good cooperation with our colleagues says Dr. Dobric."

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Grubor, do you recognise this person in the freeze?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: No, actually, I don't. He -- if he was at the time in hospital, he must be shorter period of time in hospital if I don't -- if I can't remember his face.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Dr. Dobric: For the most part this is gratifying work. It's work I hope I have performed well and I hope that I will continue. "Journalist: We are touring the hospital wards during lunchtime, the same food, pasta with beans, for Croatian soldiers and Serb civilians alike. Dr. Klaric is showing to us the modern medical equipment that is available in just one other hospital in Croatia. The new hospital in Zagreb. In the well-appointed intensive care unit no one pays any heed to the patients ethnicity. The treatment is excellent. I have no complaints. "Journalist: Any fears, misgivings? "Mr. Zubic: No, none. "Journalist: One baby was born. There is another expectant mother at the UNCRO barracks. Maybe she will follow in Mirjana's footsteps and the hospital will get a fourth born, gynecology. At any rate people will be needing treatment for a long time to come not only from wounds and diseases but also mistrust and prejudice the first step has been taken."

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And I have two other questions, or, rather, subjects that I would like to discuss but Mrs. Grubor. You said that after a certain period of time you returned to your flat. You saw that the flat had been broken into and that certain items taken, rather, stolen from your flat. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you file a report with the police station in Knin with regard to this burglary?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Well, at the time I took all my strength and courage to get out for about half an hour of the UN camp. I was scared to death to come out of the UN camp, and definitely not. I did not fail report to the local police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Mikulicic, we have now heard that the baby was 52 centimetres and it seemed in very good shape. Any question about the video you just played? Is there any issue between the parties as to the quality of the medical care before and after these events, because that's what it's all about, isn't it? I mean, if you play such a video, I take it that it is in order to put some questions to the witness in relation to that and not to tell the Court that apart from this first baby there was another one expected to be born, which of course is an enjoyable thing, but I'm asking what we're doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my intention was to have the witness identify Dr. Dobric, who is one of the Serbian doctors who stayed on to work in the hospital. And on the other hand, I wanted to demonstrate that the hospital had established a regular manner of operation, and as a result it was not necessary for the doctors employed in the hospital not to return to the hospital because they were afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that an issue in this case? May I ask the Prosecution whether there's -- is the position of the Prosecution that there was any problem in providing medical care, perhaps in return of --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I don't believe that that's one of the issues in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Mikulicic, let's try to focus on what are the real issues. Apart from -- I think the witness did not testify this doctor, did she? She did not recognise him, if I followed her testimony well. Shall we -- we could have stopped there instead of going on with the second baby. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In your statement, Ms. Grubor, that you gave in 1998, I'm referring to page 5, the penultimate paragraph on that page, in that paragraph you mentioned an incident that occurred to Mr. Drpa Dusan. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You said that Mr. Drpa went to town to get a certificate of citizenship, a so-called domovnica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And after that he returned and said that he had been to his house and that he had been beaten up by Croatian soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did he perhaps tell you how this incident during which he was beaten up occurred?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: No, he did not. However, I know he told me that his intention was to get certificate of citizenship and stay to live in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Ms. Grubor, let me try to refresh your memory to the extent that it is possible now given all the time that has elapsed. Did Mr. Drpa say anything about the fact that the Croatian soldiers found ammunition for a rifle and a pistol, and they found dynamite that was hidden in a shed? Did he say anything about that and about the fact that that's how he was finally beaten up?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: No, did he not say that. However, I have to say that during the wartime I don't think there was any house without weapons in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer, Ms. Grubor. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mikulicic. Mr. Hedaraly, let me first check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can I have D75 back up on the screen, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can did to the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Ms. Grubor, you were shown this document not too long ago, just after the break, and I just wanted to clarify something, and correct me if I'm wrong. My understanding of your testimony was that you left the hospital before the Croatian soldiers entered the underground floor.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So when -- when in the third paragraph it says: "As the soldiers stormed into the said ward, one of the nurses escaped through the exit door leaving the rest inside," is that referring to you or could it be someone else?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: It could be mistaken for me, but I left before they came downstairs to the shelter. I left as soon as I hear the explosion upstairs. They had no chance to have sighting of me at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only other thing that I have is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have, however, a question in relation to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This appears to be a redacted document. Usually it is explained to the Chamber why it is that the Chamber cannot see the whole of the document. The party that tendered it or the party that originally provided it is equally in a position to explain this to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I tendered it, Your Honour. Unfortunately, I have to say that I just used what I received from the Prosecution, so I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it you want to know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I want to know everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour at this moment I can't answer your question but we'll make sure to see if there is an unredacted version and send to the Defence and perhaps switch the exhibit if necessary as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is such an obvious question, of course, that the Chamber would have appreciated the parties would have considered it before the Chamber asked for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. We were not planning on tendering it so I understand your concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's understood. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I just have one last issue and it's with respect to the video that was played, that was D68 where we saw Mr. Jejina, I believe, talking without the sound, and the Defence has provided us what they say was spoken, and I would like to read that into the record while waiting that the Defence will get us the actual video and we will double-check so that we can have the whole exhibit on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I guess I need a foundation for why the audio is relevant. I mean, I guess --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber will have to decide on the relevance of the audio, then of course the Chamber would first have to know what the audio is. Otherwise we could not even decide upon the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine. The reason -- as I said before, Your Honours, we tendered it just to show what the basement looked like not for the content of what was being said in order to avoid having to ask more questions and examination about the substance of the content.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that was perfectly clear, and I then said if the Prosecution would find something interest in the audio that they will certainly come back to that and that's what they are doing now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And I think it is going to answer the Chamber's question about the relative timing when the video taken. I think it will be some assistance with that. If I may just read: "Operating theatre must be put in the cellar because it's very dangerous to work upstairs because of great bombing of city of Knin and near area. More than three hours Knin is shelled and a lot of wounded, especially civilian, is in the city." That concludes what we have received from the Defence, and they have said they were going to give us the original audio, and we'll be able to check that. That's all I have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I take it that -- yes. You would like to have this on the record, and I take it that's a bit of a problem, of course. Are you now providing the evidence? I mean, we have now the video without audio, so the audio is now added. I take it that you then, one of these days, will come up with the transcript of a relevant portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We have not been provided the video with the audio which is a problem, Your Honours, so for now this is the best we can do and as soon as we receive it from Mr. Misetic, we will introduce it in the best possible manner so that the audio version is also in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then of course what we should do is ask the witness having heard those words spoken whether this is also your understanding of why to some extent you've answered the question already, why the surgical activity took place in the basement. Thank you for that answer. I have one more question for you if it was for the Prosecution, Mr. Hedaraly. Could we have P58 on the screen again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I believe the answer the witness was to your question was not recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: She confirmed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if there's one additional matter, I apologise, Your Honour. P59 was marked but I believe we have not tendered it into evidence and exhibit the short clips, if we would do that at this stage, the second sentence with the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection to 59?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then P59 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, as long as we're on D75 the redacted document, part page 3 of that document is also redacted so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that will all redactions are taken care of and formally tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could we move into the left upper corner. Yes, that portion. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Grubor, you -- we read from this document which was marked by you and of course this is now the new version, that 17 indicates the direction from which Knin was shelled from the direction of Dinara. You also marked on this document where the main entrance to the hospital was, that is with an arrow and a 15.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I earlier asked you whether the portions we had seen from the outside of the building, whether these were portions that were also portions that were exposed to fire. Now, comparing arrow 17 with the entrance of the building, apparently being little bit -- a little bit --

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Exposed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to the north, I would from these arrows, I would expect that the wall in which the main entrance is located would be exposed at least to the shelling of -- from the direction of 17. I'm just trying to understand your testimony in detail. Is this understanding -- would you consider that there's -- it's understandable?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: That's -- this arrow here, as well as the other one that I drew from the south direction is my presumption. I am not 100 per cent sure. I mean, if we had probably aerial photo of the mountains around probably I could give exact. However, I can't tell exactly what exact direction was as mostly I would assume by sound, not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: -- by seeing bombs flying by some certain direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now Dinara appears to be a place which is known what the location of that place is, or is it a wider area which could explain why the arrow might be a bit different from what we see here or would be a range rather than a single arrow?

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Really, I would not know exactly what location was where the bombings were coming from. However, I did hear the hissing noise coming from that direction, but it's hard to be precise if someone ask me where exactly. As I said previously, I'm not expert. I tried to give as much as I can in my recollection, which is not 100 per cent accurate in terms of bombs falling or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: -- some -- some -- something that I was not directly there observing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I fully understand that. But I just wanted to tell you that I had some difficulties in reconciling your evidence that the walls we've seen would not be the walls exposed to fire, whereas from these arrows it appears that the entrance faces approximately north-east, whereas the arrow from where this part of the fire came is east or north-east which is rather similar.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: I mean, regardless of that, I did see a few bombs exploding on the hospital grounds on the north side. So I wouldn't be able to tell where they were coming from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you are aware on this map that north is to the left and not as usual.

utterances.speaker: MIRA GRUBOR
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I have in further questions. Any need for further questions triggered by the questions of the Bench? If not, Ms. Grubor, I would like to thank you for coming to The Hague. I often say to come a far distance Hague, but I think in this case it was really very far.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Distance. Thank you very much for taking the effort to come to The Hague and for answering the questions of both parties and the bench, and I wish you although it may be a long trip but at least a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is no time left at this moment to further deal with the MFIs which we started last Friday. I'm looking to the Prosecution. Tomorrow's witness, no special problems?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. He is here and he is ready to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we will adjourn, and we will resume tomorrow, the 15th of April, at 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom III.
